bib.title: Beyond Entangled Planning: Task-Decoupled Planning for Long-Horizon Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Beyond Entangled Planning: Task-Decoupled Planning for Long-Horizon Agents", Yunfan Li, Bingbing Xu, Xueyun Tian, Xiucheng Xu, Huawei Shen (ICT-CAS and UCAS). arXiv 2601.07577v1, 12 Jan 2026. The PDF shows no venue, so call it a preprint. The format looks like an ACL-style submission.

COVERAGE: 56,103 of 56,103 chars read. That covers the body, limitations, references, appendices A to C and all six prompt templates. The Figure 1 to 4 images were not rendered. I used the text captions only.

FIT WARNING: moderate. The paper is directly on topic for separating planning from execution, plan-and-execute against ReAct, and decomposition. Three things limit it.
- It adds a Supervisor and a DAG, so it is more than plain plan-and-execute.
- The token-cost evidence compares only against Plan-and-Act, not ReAct.
- The samples are small and there is no variance reporting.

Use it as one design point on "scope the context per subtask", not as proof that decoupling beats ReAct.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. TDP uses far fewer output tokens than Plan-and-Act while scoring higher.
   - number: 82.4% and 82.1% reduction on HotpotQA (1,747.47 and 1,361.62 tokens). 74.5% and 70.4% on ScienceWorld (5,060.57 and 5,461.65 tokens).
   - setup: average output tokens only. DeepSeek-V3.2 and GPT-4o. 100 HotpotQA and 100 ScienceWorld instances. Plan-and-Act is the only comparator. Input tokens and call counts are not reported.
   - quote: "On HotpotQA, TDP uses 1,747.47 average output tokens with DeepSeek-V3.2 and 1,361.62 with GPT-4o, corresponding to an 82.4% and 82.1% reduction compared to Plan-and-Act. On ScienceWorld, TDP uses 5,060.57 average output tokens with DeepSeek-V3.2 and 5,461.65 with GPT-4o, reducing by 74.5% and 70.4% respectively."
   - where: §4.3, Figure 3, around char 24,500.
2. The authors attribute the saving to confined replanning. Plan-and-Act revises a global plan, while TDP revises only the active node. This is an explanation and was not ablated.
   - number: none
   - quote: "Plan-and-Act resolves deviations by revising a global plan, which tends to expand the replanning scope and repeatedly re-justify decisions that are not causally affected by the current state."
   - where: §4.3.
3. On TravelPlanner, TDP has the best Avg of the four methods under both models, and it leads hard-constraint micro pass under DeepSeek.
   - number: Avg 34% against ReAct 30%, CoT 28%, Plan-and-Act 25% (DeepSeek). Avg 30% against 28%, 25%, 26% (GPT-4o). Hard-constraint micro 32.5% against 15%, 10%, 10% (DeepSeek).
   - setup: 120 validation tasks, 40 each from easy, medium and hard. 50-step cap. Final Pass is 0 to 0.83% for every method, so it is about 1 task of 120. The Avg margins are 2 to 4 points on 120 tasks, with no seeds or confidence intervals.
   - quote: "TDP achieves the best Avg score under both DeepSeek-V3.2 (34%) and GPT-4o (30%)" and "TDP achieves the highest micro pass rate on hard constraints (32.5%) under DeepSeek-V3.2"
   - where: §4.2 and Table 1.
4. Interleaved ReAct stays competitive or better where feedback is immediate, namely ScienceWorld.
   - number: DeepSeek reward ReAct 58.26 against TDP 56.17. GPT-4o reward TDP 53.24 against ReAct 50.63.
   - setup: 100 test instances, 60-step cap, dense reward 0 to 1 as the paper describes it. The table shows values like 58.26, so it is probably scaled to 0-100. The text does not say.
   - quote: "TDP achieves the best average reward under GPT-4o (53.24) and remains highly competitive with ReAct under DeepSeek-V3.2"
   - where: §4.2, Table 1. The paper says the environment "naturally favors step-wise planning paradigms such as ReAct".
5. HotpotQA: TDP gives the best accuracy-when-delivered (Deli. Acc.), but plain accuracy is about equal to ReAct.
   - number: Deli. Acc. 85.88% (TDP) against 73.47% (ReAct) under DeepSeek. 82.14% against 73% under GPT-4o per the table. Accuracy 73% against 72% (DeepSeek). 69% against ReAct 73% (GPT-4o).
   - setup: 100 dev-fullwiki instances, 30-step cap, Qwen-MAX as LLM judge. Interactive Wikipedia with Search, Lookup and Finish actions.
   - quote: "TDP achieves the strongest delivered-answer quality under DeepSeek-V3.2 (85.88%)"
   - where: §4.2 and Table 1.
   - caveat: Deli. Acc. is conditioned on delivery, so it excludes tasks that never finished. The text does not define delivery rate for HotpotQA. Plain accuracy is the fairer number.
6. One-shot planning with no replanning (CoT with an initial plan) is the weakest at delivering. Plan-and-Act also lowers delivery on TravelPlanner.
   - number: delivery 91% (CoT) and 82.50% (Plan-and-Act) against ReAct 100% (DeepSeek). GPT-4o: 75.83% and 59.17% against 95.83%. TDP 96.67% and 94.17%.
   - setup: TravelPlanner, 50-step cap, 120 tasks.
   - quote: none verbatim for these figures. The values come from Table 1, which extracts as a flat row. The column mapping is my reading.
   - where: Table 1.
7. Design: a Supervisor builds a DAG of subtasks. A Planner and Executor see only the node spec, predecessor outputs and that node's own trace. Replanning is node-local. A Self-Revision step edits the DAG after each batch of ready nodes.
   - number: none
   - quote: "They never consume the full global execution history and sub-task decoupling is realized by this explicit context scoping."
   - where: §3.3.

BASELINES
- Three baselines, each run with DeepSeek-V3.2 and GPT-4o: ReAct, "CoT with an initial plan" (one-shot, no replanning) and Plan-and-Act (high-level plan plus step-wise execution, with replanning).
- Matching is on the step cap only: 30 for HotpotQA, 60 for ScienceWorld, 50 for TravelPlanner. The paper says "matched settings" without details.
- Tokens and LLM calls are not matched. Cost is reported only for TDP against Plan-and-Act, as output tokens only. There is no cost figure for ReAct or CoT, none for TravelPlanner, and no call counts.
- TDP makes an extra Supervisor call after every environment step, because the status evaluation runs per step. That overhead is not itemised, so the saving may rest on output tokens alone.

LIMITS
- Authors concede two things. Subtask granularity "may not always be strictly optimized for execution efficiency". Evaluation is on verifiable benchmarks only, not open-ended tasks.
- Not shown: no ablations of Supervisor, Self-Revision or scoping, so the causal claim is untested. There is no seed variance and no significance test. There is no comparison to stronger baselines such as ReCode or HiPlan, which are cited but not run. There is no wall-clock latency and no cost on TravelPlanner. Only two models were tested, DeepSeek-V3.2 and GPT-4o. The LLM judge is Qwen-MAX.
- Samples are small: 100, 100 and 120 tasks.
- The abstract's "up to 82%" is the best case, and it applies to output tokens against Plan-and-Act only.

BUILDS ON
- ReAct (Yao et al., 2022).
- Plan-and-Act (Erdogan et al., 2025), the main baseline.
- Pre-Act (Rawat et al., 2025).
- ReCode (Yu et al., 2025).
- Related work credited: GoalAct (Chen et al., 2025), HiPlan (Li et al., 2025b), AdaPlanner (Sun et al., 2023), MPO (Xiong et al., 2025), Decomposed Prompting (Khot et al., 2022), Least-to-Most (Zhou et al., 2022) and HuggingGPT (Shen et al., 2023).
- Benchmarks: TravelPlanner (Xie et al., 2024), ScienceWorld (Wang et al., 2022a) and HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018).

CODE (prompts worth keeping, in Appendix C, about chars 41,000 to 56,000)
- Algorithm 1 (§4.1). It is a nested loop: `N ← GetExecutableNodes(G)`, then for each node `π_i ← P(n_i)`. Inside, `a ← Ex(π_i,H)`, `o ← E.Step(a)` and `⟨d_i, r_i, H⟩ ← Sup.eval(n_i,o,H)`. If `replan`, `π_i ← P.refine(n_i,o,H)`. After the batch, `G ← Sup.update(G)`.
- The DAG construction output schema:
  ```
  {"subgoals":[{"id":"node_1","description":"Subgoal description (semantic level)","dependencies":[]}]}
  ```
  The prompt rule is "Create subgoals at semantic task level. Each subgoal represents a complete task unit".
- The Supervisor evaluation schema, with a bias against replanning: `{"status": "<completed|failed|needs_more_steps>", "reason": ..., "need_replan": <true or false>}`. The prompt line is "MINIMIZE replanning. Set need_replan to true ONLY if:". On `needs_more_steps` without replan, the reason field carries 1 to 2 sentences of guidance for the Executor.
- The Planner prompt scopes the subgoal: "Focus ONLY on the subgoal above. Do NOT plan for other parts of the task." It also says "Describe WHAT needs to be accomplished, not HOW".
- The Executor prompt ends with "Output ONLY the action string, nothing else."
- The DAG update prompt allows only three operations: update descriptions, extend, remove. It says "If executable nodes = 0, you MUST add new nodes".

FIGURES
- Figure 1 (page 2). It compares step-wise ReAct, one-shot planning and TDP on one TravelPlanner task. This is the best candidate for the chapter, because it shows the three architectures side by side.
- Figure 2 is the TDP overview.
- Figure 3 is the cost bar chart: output tokens and performance for Plan-and-Act against TDP.
- Figure 4 is the case study. Node 3 does not inherit Node 2's flight-search trace, and replanning stays inside Node 2.
- I did not run the figure script, so these captions are paraphrased from the extracted text.

PROBLEMS
- Table 1 extracted as flat text. The mapping of columns is inferred: Delivery, CS Micro, CS Macro, HC Micro, HC Macro, Final Pass, Avg, then HotpotQA Accuracy, Deli. Acc., Avg, then ScienceWorld Reward.
- Table 1's "Avg" for TravelPlanner appears as a percentage. Check it against the PDF image before quoting it.
- The text says TDP "matches the best-performing methods on GPT-4o (20.0%)" for hard-constraint micro. In the table, Plan-and-Act has 20.00%, ReAct 15.00%, and TDP 20.00%.
- The text claims TDP "preserves strong completion behavior ... not driven by selective answering", but gives no delivery numbers for HotpotQA.
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
